title: Prime ideals and convex subgroups of a valuation ring
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $A\subseteq K$ be a valuation ring, meaning that for every $a\in K^\times$ at least one of $a,a^{-1}$ lies in $A$. Put $\Gamma=K^\times/A^\times$ and order $\Gamma$ by $[x]\le [y]$ when $y/x\in A$. A subgroup $H\le\Gamma$ is convex if whenever $h_1\le g\le h_2$ with $h_1,h_2\in H$, then $g\in H$. Then the prime ideals of $A$, ordered by inclusion, are canonically order anti-isomorphic to the convex subgroups of $\Gamma$, ordered by inclusion. In particular, every strict chain of $n$ inclusions of prime ideals in $A$ yields a strict chain of $n$ inclusions of convex subgroups of $\Gamma$.

proof.text: The valuation-ring alternative applied to any quotient y/x makes the relation [x]≤[y] total; multiplying representatives by units does not change membership in A, and multiplication in K^× descends to the quotient. Thus Γ is a totally ordered abelian group and the value-group notation in the statement is well defined. The subgroup H is convex exactly when it contains every element lying between two of its elements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-valuation-ring-ideal-correspondence]. It gives an inclusion-preserving bijection between ideals of A and ideals of Γ, and carries prime ideals of A to prime ideals of the positive cone Γ_{≥0}.

Apply [lem-trf-ordered-group-prime-ideal-convex-correspondence] to Γ. Its formulas I_H={γ≥0:γ∉H} and H_I={γ:|γ|∉I} are inverse; upward closure and primality make H_I a subgroup and convex, while convexity makes I_H a prime ideal. Inclusion is reversed, so this is an order anti-isomorphism from prime positive-cone ideals to convex subgroups.

proof.text: Composing the inclusion-preserving prime correspondence of Step 2 with the order anti-isomorphism of Step 3 gives the claimed canonical order anti-isomorphism between prime ideals of A and convex subgroups of Γ. An order anti-isomorphism sends every strict chain of n inclusions to a strict chain of n inclusions, proving the final assertion.

lean.statement: theorem primeSpectrum_orderDualEquiv_convexSubgroup {K : Type u} [Field K] (A : ValuationSubring K) : ∃ ord : LinearOrder (Kˣ ⧸ A.unitGroup), (∀ x y : Kˣ, ord.le (QuotientGroup.mk' A.unitGroup x) (QuotientGroup.mk' A.unitGroup y) ↔ (y : K) / (x : K) ∈ A) ∧ (∀ a b c : Kˣ ⧸ A.unitGroup, ord.le a b → ord.le (a * c) (b * c)) ∧ ∃ e : (PrimeSpectrum A)ᵒᵈ ≃o {H : Subgroup (Kˣ ⧸ A.unitGroup) // ∀ ⦃h₁ h₂ g : Kˣ ⧸ A.unitGroup⦄, h₁ ∈ H → h₂ ∈ H → ord.le h₁ g → ord.le g h₂ → g ∈ H}, (∀ (P : PrimeSpectrum A) (x : Kˣ) (hx : (x : K) ∈ A), QuotientGroup.mk' A.unitGroup x ∈ (e (OrderDual.toDual P)).1 ↔ (⟨(x : K), hx⟩ : A) ∉ P.asIdeal) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (p : Fin (n + 1) → PrimeSpectrum A), StrictMono p → StrictAnti (fun i : Fin (n + 1) ↦ e (OrderDual.toDual (p i))))
